papers.title: Finite Certificates and Undecidable Gibbs Uniqueness
papers.subject: Mathematical physics
papers.summary: Even at a fixed positive temperature, no algorithm can decide whether a finite-range classical spin model has a unique Gibbs state. Finite computation certificates select a phase through exact cancellation, while the unique equilibrium still has exponentially decaying correlations.
papers.abstract: We construct translation-invariant classical interactions on ℤ² for which deciding uniqueness among all Gibbs states is undecidable at inverse temperature one. The finite on-site alphabet depends effectively on the input; interaction supports are fixed, and local energy terms take only the integer values 0, 1, 20. Exact character orthogonality converts a strictly positive finite-energy model into a gas of finite computation histories. A halting certificate produces a uniformly positive phase-selection bias, however small. A reference Ising comparison and an independent-disagreement argument then give uniqueness and exponential clustering of every local physical observable. Without halting, the entire Gibbs simplex is affinely isomorphic to the two-dimensional zero-field Ising simplex. A distinct soft-certificate construction has the same dichotomy for one table at every finite inverse temperature at least 2/5. We prove boundary-specific exponential convergence, smooth pressure with summable cumulants on the uniqueness branch, uniform computability of the selected phase and its right pressure jet, and stability under small finite-range spin perturbations. An effective compactness argument supplies a computable valid convergence modulus for each unique computable finite-range specification; the impossibility concerns total bounds across the undecidable family. Exact microscopic symmetrization excludes a family-wide perturbation radius for arbitrary real interactions.
papers.description: Even at a fixed positive temperature, no algorithm can decide whether a finite-range classical spin model has a unique Gibbs state. Finite computation certificates select a phase through exact cancellation, while the unique equilibrium still has exponentially decaying correlations.

papers.title: Fixed-format undecidability of exact catalytic tensor restriction
papers.subject: Quantum information and algebraic complexity
papers.status: AI-generated proof candidate; independent validation and priority review pending
papers.summary: A rank-drop construction connects exact quantum catalysis with algebra representations, giving a route to undecidability within a fixed positive tensor family.
papers.abstract: A proposed representation compiler links finite-dimensional representations of finitely presented rational associative algebras to exact stochastic restriction of three-tensors with an exactly returned bipartite maximally entangled catalyst. Rank-drop markers constrain otherwise unrestricted local maps. The resulting construction gives a route to recursively enumerable complete conversion along a fixed rank-one affine family of strictly positive integer tensors, together with a finite example of genuine catalysis. The model concerns exact conversion with unbounded catalyst dimension; it imposes no uniform positive success probability.

papers.title: Thermal balance and the amplifier entropy photon-number inequality
papers.contribution: Harjas Sandhu developed and coordinated the agentic system used for this investigation. The mathematical development and writing are AI-generated; no human mathematical authorship is assigned.
papers.subject: Quantum information and mathematical physics
papers.rights_notice: The source bundle retains the Apache License 2.0 and attribution notice for incorporated OpenAI material. See LICENSE and NOTICE.txt for scope.
papers.abstract: The entropy photon number is the occupation of a thermal state with a given entropy per mode. We give a variational argument for its sharp lower bound under amplification of two independent finite-energy inputs, allowing correlations within each input group. The proof turns on an agreement of signs: the creation port reverses a logarithmic-mean metric, and thermal relaxation obeys the corresponding signed occupation balance. At a regularized entropy minimum, these two facts cancel the energy corrections and force the thermal-balance defects to vanish. A trace-norm Stein bound, obtained from thermal-attenuator smoothing, then closes the argument. We also give a Gaussian spectral refinement, characterize Gaussian equality by a common symplectic shape, and deduce a sharp correlation bound for the two outputs. The conjecture is due to De Palma, Mari and Giovannetti; the variational framework and four-weight interpolation are adapted from OpenAI's beam-splitter argument.

The mathematical development and writing are AI-generated; established contributions are credited in the text.

papers.title: An example of a non-sofic hyperbolic group
papers.subject: Group theory
papers.abstract: We construct a torsion-free, two-dimensional, word-hyperbolic group which is not sofic. Our construction builds on OpenAI's construction of a non-residually finite hyperbolic group, see OpenAI 252.
papers.provenance: This paper is based on an AI-generated construction obtained by Harjas Sandhu on October 7, 2026, which was in turn based on the OpenAI breakthrough [14]. The second author worked through the proof to make it readable and to reduce unnecessary overhead.
papers.provenance_summary: The construction inherits marked lines, triangular relations, an interpolation identity and comparisons of real and finite-field ranks from OpenAI 252. The acknowledgments also disclose AI assistance in drafting and explain how the paper relates these ingredients to earlier mathematics. The PDF hosted here is the unchanged arXiv v1 preprint.

papers.title: Complete information orders of quantum channels: equivalence and undecidability
papers.contribution: Harjas Sandhu developed and coordinated the agentic system used for these investigations and serves as the manuscript contact, rather than as a scientific author.
papers.subject: Quantum information

companion.description: The companion preprint develops capacity and one-way distillation consequences that depend on the order results presented here.

papers.abstract: With arbitrary finite quantum references, relative entropy, Holevo information and SLD Fisher information induce the same channel order, reversed by complementation. This order is coRE-complete, even for strictly positive rational POVMs. Its bounded entropy defect is additive and uncomputable at every fixed positive additive accuracy.

papers.summary: Relative entropy, Holevo information and Fisher information define the same complete quantum-channel order. Even strictly positive rational measurements leave that comparison undecidable.

papers.title: From complete channel order to capacity and one-way distillation
papers.contribution: Harjas Sandhu developed and coordinated the agentic system used for these investigations and serves as the manuscript contact, rather than as a scientific author.
papers.subject: Quantum information

companion.description: This manuscript develops capacity and distillation consequences using the complete-order results of the companion preprint.

papers.abstract: A flagged channel with a four-dimensional auxiliary input turns every failed complete information comparison into positive private and quantum capacity. This transfers complete-order undecidability to exact-zero capacity and one-way distillation, even under any prescribed two-way distillation lower bound. All reference transmission and activation use the constructed channel itself.
